title: Eleven Yards and One Shirt
subtitle: 仪表穿着 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 仪表穿着（生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）
meta: 主题语境：仪表穿着（生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）　|　核心词汇：cotton　|　正文 329 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cotton 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 my grandmother ① bought a cotton that shrank in the first wash, and she said the buying was the whole of the sewing. The ② cotton, meaning the cloth and not the plant, ran eleven yards and stayed that length until the water; cotton, she said, is the only thing in a dress that is judged by how much it gives back.

Every ③ cotton in that drawer had the same label, and the ④ cotton at the end, meaning the one she kept for the shirts and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever ironed twice. Cotton, my mother said, is nine parts label and one part somebody willing to iron; my grandmother said the ironing is the part that fills eleven yards.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the cotton was the whole of the field, meaning the crop and not the cloth. The ⑥ cotton, meaning the crop and not any of that, is the only thing in a field that everybody wears and nobody sows; cotton, he said, is either something you buy or the only word that means both a cloth and a crop. She said the crop is the part they remember.

By 1967 the ⑦ cotton had become a line in an order, and the order had become an argument about the label. The ⑧ cotton of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in August, was one wash and thirty years of ironing; cotton, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to iron. He said the ironing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cotton I remember is the one at the end, which she bought in 1973 and is still described as the softest in the county. A ⑩ cotton, my mother said in 1975, is the only thing that improves by being washed; every cotton, she said, is a crop that has agreed to look like a cloth. She said the crop was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 棉布（指那块布本身，与那种植物相对）
C. 固定搭配：buy a cotton 买一块棉布
D. n. 棉布（指那个抽屉里每一块）
E. n. 棉布（指末尾那一块）
F. n. 棉花；棉株（指田里的作物）
G. n. 棉布（指订单里提到的那一块）
H. n. 棉；棉质（抽象总称）

items.q: bought a cotton that shrank in the first wash
The cotton, meaning the cloth and not the plant
the cotton was the whole of the field
the cotton had become a line in an order
The cotton of the whole thing
A cotton, my mother said in 1975

answers.why: buy a cotton 意为“买一块棉布”，1959 年祖母买了一块头一次下水就缩水的棉布。
cotton 意为“棉布”，指那块布本身而不是那种植物，有十一码长。
cotton 指那个抽屉里每一块棉布，每一块都缝着同样的标签。
cotton 指末尾那一块（她留给衬衫的那一块），是唯一有人熨过两次的。
cotton 意为“棉花、棉株”，父亲说棉花就是那片田的全部，指的是田里的作物而不是那块布。
cotton 为另一个义项，指田里的棉花作物而不是那块布，是田里人人都穿在身上、却无人播种的东西。
cotton 意为“棉布”，指订单里提到的那一块，到 1967 年这块棉布成了订单里的一行。
cotton 意为“棉、棉质”，祖母八月写道，整件事的棉质是一次下水三十年的熨烫。
cotton 意为“棉布”，我记得的是末尾那一块，她 1973 年买的，至今仍被说成全县最软的。
cotton 为抽象总称，母亲说一块棉布是唯一会因为被水洗而变好的东西。
